newsitem.title: USA: GM says 19,958 U.S., Mexican workers idled.
newsitem.headline: GM says 19,958 U.S., Mexican workers idled.

text.p: General Motors Corp said as of 11:00 EST Thursday, 19,958 of its U.S. and Mexican employees are still idled as a result of a strike by the Canadian Auto Workers Union that ended last week.
It said vehicle assembly facilities at Buick City, Flint, Mich. and Fairfax, Kan. are returning to full operation on Thursday.
"We will not speculate on when the remaining workers in the U.S. affected by the Canadian work stoppage will return to their operations," GM said in a statement.
On Wednesday, GM had 23,158 North American workers idled due to shortages of Canadian-made parts.
The company also said a total of 9,809 U.S. GM employees were affected by work stoppages called by the United Auto Workers union.

That number increased increased from 7,559 on Wednesday with the addition of 2,250 workers from the company's Fort Wayne, Ind. plant which makes Chevrolet and GMC full-size pickup trucks. Besides Fort Wayne, affected GM operations include Indianapolis, Ind. (metal fabrication) and Janesville, Wis. (assembly).
